meta.scope: Ecuador batch 1 — Phase 0+1. Core national statistical system from INEC catalogue top-down: institutional identity, ENEMDU (labour + poverty), IPC, national accounts anchors, and Banco Central del Ecuador. Definition locked.

candidates.title: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INEC) — institutional statistical identity
candidates.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos
candidates.description: National statistical office of Ecuador. Produces the core official statistics (prices, labour force, poverty, national accounts inputs, census, etc.) and coordinates the national statistical system.
referenced_by: All major INEC programme methodologies and technical bulletins
Banco Central del Ecuador statistical publications that cite INEC sources
candidates.notes: Institutional parent node for Ecuadorian official statistics. Continuously cited as the producer of the principal economic and social series.

candidates.title: Encuesta Nacional de Empleo, Desempleo y Subempleo (ENEMDU)
candidates.description: Continuous household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators (adequate employment, underemployment, unemployment) and for income-based poverty and inequality measurement. National, urban and rural domains.
candidates.notes: Central social and labour survey. Monthly and quarterly releases. Official source for both labour statistics and monetary poverty. Recent (Dec 2025): national poverty 21.4%, extreme poverty 8.3%; unemployment ~2.6–3.6%.

candidates.title: Pobreza por ingresos y pobreza extrema / Income poverty
candidates.description: Official income-poverty and extreme-poverty incidence, calculated by comparing household per-capita income (from ENEMDU) with nationally defined poverty lines updated by the IPC. Published with urban/rural breakdowns.
candidates.notes: Headline social indicator. Dec 2025: national poverty 21.4% (down sharply from 28.0% a year earlier); extreme poverty 8.3%. Large urban–rural gap (urban ~13.8%, rural ~37.6%).

candidates.title: Líneas de pobreza y pobreza extrema
candidates.description: Monetary values of the poverty and extreme-poverty lines (per capita), updated with the IPC.
candidates.notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. Dec 2025: poverty line ~USD 92.40 per person; extreme poverty line ~USD 52.07.

candidates.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
candidates.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services.
candidates.notes: Flagship price statistic. Used to update the poverty lines and as the primary inflation indicator for the dollarized economy and for BCE analysis.

candidates.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Ecuador
candidates.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income. Quarterly and annual releases.
candidates.notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. In Ecuador the Banco Central plays a larger role in national accounts compilation than in pure INEI/DANE-style systems.

candidates.title: Banco Central del Ecuador — statistical publications (monetary, external, inflation)
candidates.description: Central-bank statistical output covering monetary aggregates, balance of payments, international reserves, and macroeconomic analysis. Operates in a fully dollarized monetary regime.
candidates.notes: In the Ecuadorian division of labour INEC leads labour, poverty and prices; the BCE leads national accounts, external sector and financial statistics. Dollarization means there is no independent policy interest rate of the classic type.

candidates.title: Empleo adecuado / pleno empleo (ENEMDU)
candidates.description: Key labour-market indicator from ENEMDU measuring the share of the employed who work full-time at or above the minimum wage. Central quality-of-employment metric in the Ecuadorian system.
candidates.notes: Distinctive Ecuadorian labour indicator. Dec 2025: national adequate employment 37.1% (up from 33.0% a year earlier). Large urban–rural gap (urban ~46%, rural ~20%).

candidates.title: Censo de Población y Vivienda / Population and Housing Census
candidates.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline and sampling frames for household surveys.
candidates.notes: Foundational demographic product. Continuously cited by ENEMDU design and poverty analysis.

candidates.title: Coeficiente de Gini / Income inequality
candidates.description: Official Gini coefficient of income inequality, calculated from the same ENEMDU income concept used for monetary poverty.
candidates.notes: Companion inequality indicator to the poverty series. Recent values in the mid-0.44 to 0.47 range.

proposed_edges.basis: Income poverty is calculated from ENEMDU household income data.
Poverty status is determined by comparing per-capita income with the official poverty lines.
Poverty lines are updated with the IPC.
Adequate employment is a core indicator derived from the ENEMDU.
The Gini coefficient is computed from the same income distribution underlying the poverty estimates.
ENEMDU is a core continuous survey of INEC.
IPC is produced and disseminated by INEC.
